Miles Davis：独特音色、双重教育与音乐遗产未作答标题匹配 · 3 段 · 403 词 · 3 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

本材料也用于本册教学。已看过原文、示范或答案时，这次作答用于练习与复习，不作为未见题测试。

官方样题 · British Council · Academic Practice Test 2 · Miles Davis · Q14–19 · PDF 第 1, 2 页

Choose the correct heading for each paragraph from the list of headings. Write the correct Roman numeral, i–ix. 本组保留原题号；同一标题不可重复使用。

AAt the age of thirteen, Miles Davis was given his first trumpet, lessons were arranged with a local trumpet player, and a musical odyssey began. These early lessons, paid for and supported by his father, had a profound effect on shaping Davis’ signature sound. Whereas most trumpeters of the era favoured the use of vibrato (a wobbly quiver in pitch inflected in the instrument’s tone), Davis was taught to play with a long, straight tone, a preference his instructor reportedly drilled into the young trumpeter with a rap on the knuckles every time Davis began using vibrato. This clear, distinctive style never left Davis. He continued playing with it for the rest of his career, once remarking, ‘If I can’t get that sound, I can’t play anything.’

BHaving graduated from high school in 1944, Davis moved to New York City, where he continued his musical education both in the clubs and in the classroom. His enrolment in the prestigious Julliard School of Music was short-lived, however – he soon dropped out, criticising what he perceived as an over-emphasis on the classical European repertoire and a neglect of jazz. Davis did later acknowledge, however, that this time at the school was invaluable in terms of developing his trumpet-playing technique and giving him a solid grounding in music theory. Much of his early training took place in the form of jam sessions and performances in the clubs of 52nd Street, where he played alongside both up- and-coming and established members of the jazz pantheon such as Coleman Hawkins, Eddie ‘Lockjaw’ Davis, and Thelonious Monk.

CIn the late 1940s, Davis collaborated with nine other instrumentalists, including a French horn and a tuba player, to produce The Birth of Cool, an album now renowned for the inchoate sounds of what would later become known as ‘cool’ jazz. In contrast to popular jazz styles of the day, which featured rapid, rollicking beats, shrieking vocals, and short, sharp horn blasts, Davis’ album was the forerunner of a different kind of sound – thin, light horn-playing, hushed drums and a more restrained, formal arrangement. Although it received little acclaim at the time (the liner notes to one of Davis’ later recordings call it a ‘spectacular failure’), in hindsight The Birth of Cool has become recognised as a pivotal moment in jazz history, cementing – alongside his 1958 recording, Kind of Blue – Davis’ legacy as one of the most innovative musicians of his era.

材料精读 · 内容与词句

这三段沿着音色形成、学习经历和录音创作展开，解释戴维斯的独特风格怎样产生，以及一部当时反响冷淡的作品如何在后来获得历史地位。个人风格、不同学习环境与作品接受史是相互关联的三条线。

A

At the age of thirteen, Miles Davis was given his first trumpet, lessons were arranged with a local trumpet player, and a musical odyssey began. These early lessons, paid for and supported by his father, had a profound effect on shaping Davis’ signature sound. Whereas most trumpeters of the era favoured the use of vibrato (a wobbly quiver in pitch inflected in the instrument’s tone), Davis was taught to play with a long, straight tone, a preference his instructor reportedly drilled into the young trumpeter with a rap on the knuckles every time Davis began using vibrato. This clear, distinctive style never left Davis. He continued playing with it for the rest of his career, once remarking, ‘If I can’t get that sound, I can’t play anything.’

A段从十三岁获得小号写起。父亲资助的课程塑造了他的标志性音色：当时许多演奏者偏爱颤音，他的老师却训练他保持悠长、平直的音。后来的自述表明，这种音色成为他认同自身演奏的基础。原文描述老师敲打指关节的做法，是人物经历，不是认可这种教学方式。

B

Having graduated from high school in 1944, Davis moved to New York City, where he continued his musical education both in the clubs and in the classroom. His enrolment in the prestigious Julliard School of Music was short-lived, however – he soon dropped out, criticising what he perceived as an over-emphasis on the classical European repertoire and a neglect of jazz. Davis did later acknowledge, however, that this time at the school was invaluable in terms of developing his trumpet-playing technique and giving him a solid grounding in music theory. Much of his early training took place in the form of jam sessions and performances in the clubs of 52nd Street, where he played alongside both up- and-coming and established members of the jazz pantheon such as Coleman Hawkins, Eddie ‘Lockjaw’ Davis, and Thelonious Monk.

B段把音乐教育分为学校课堂和俱乐部两种环境。戴维斯不满学校偏重欧洲古典曲目、忽视爵士，因而退学；但他后来仍肯定学校对小号技巧和乐理基础的帮助。与新秀和成名乐手同台的经历，则提供了课堂之外的实践。两种学习来源并非互相排斥。

C

In the late 1940s, Davis collaborated with nine other instrumentalists, including a French horn and a tuba player, to produce The Birth of Cool, an album now renowned for the inchoate sounds of what would later become known as ‘cool’ jazz. In contrast to popular jazz styles of the day, which featured rapid, rollicking beats, shrieking vocals, and short, sharp horn blasts, Davis’ album was the forerunner of a different kind of sound – thin, light horn-playing, hushed drums and a more restrained, formal arrangement. Although it received little acclaim at the time (the liner notes to one of Davis’ later recordings call it a ‘spectacular failure’), in hindsight The Birth of Cool has become recognised as a pivotal moment in jazz history, cementing – alongside his 1958 recording, Kind of Blue – Davis’ legacy as one of the most innovative musicians of his era.

C段将前面的个人风格推进到合作录音。他与其他乐器演奏者创造了较轻、克制、编排更正式的声音，与当时流行的急促节拍和强烈音响形成对照。作品当时缺少赞誉，后来却被视为爵士史的重要转折。in hindsight明确区分当时反响与后来的评价。

词语与搭配

had a profound effect on

对……产生深远影响

have an effect on后接受到影响的人、事或过程；profound强调影响深而持久，此处具体指早期课程塑造音色。

a solid grounding in music theory

扎实的乐理基础

grounding表示作为后续学习或实践基础的知识训练，常与in搭配；不是地面或被禁足的意思。

In contrast to

与……形成对照

后接名词性成分，此处引出当时流行爵士与新录音在声音上的差异，不表示其中一方天然更好。

in hindsight

事后回看；从后来的认识看

用于区分经历发生时与后来回顾时的理解；不能把后来获得的评价写成当时已经普遍接受。

句子精读

Whereas most trumpeters of the era favoured the use of vibrato (a wobbly quiver in pitch inflected in the instrument’s tone), Davis was taught to play with a long, straight tone, a preference his instructor reportedly drilled into the young trumpeter with a rap on the knuckles every time Davis began using vibrato.

当时大多数小号演奏者喜欢运用颤音，即乐器音色中音高的颤动；戴维斯却被教导使用悠长、平直的音。据说，每当他开始使用颤音时，老师就敲一下他的指关节，以此把这种偏好灌输给他。

Whereas引出对照；括号解释vibrato。a preference补充说明前面的演奏取向，his instructor reportedly drilled into...说明训练方式；reportedly表明这一细节来自转述。every time引出每次发生的情形。

Davis did later acknowledge, however, that this time at the school was invaluable in terms of developing his trumpet-playing technique and giving him a solid grounding in music theory.

不过，戴维斯后来确实承认，在这所学校的经历对发展他的小号演奏技巧、打下扎实的乐理基础非常宝贵。

did强调他确实作过这一肯定；that引出承认的内容。in terms of后面developing和giving并列，指出两方面价值。this time指在学校学习的这段经历，不能因他退学就把学校贡献一并否定。

这篇材料里可用于写作的表达

a solid grounding in music theory

扎实的乐理基础

可说明专业理论如何支持实践；不把理论学习与工作实习写成只能二选一。

用于写作：自编例句，适用于本科课程是否应包括实习：音乐专业作为具体例子，说明已有理论知识怎样在工作环境中应用；不代表所有专业都需要录音棚实习。

读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。

Miles Davis：困境、跨界与创造力未作答标题匹配 · 3 段 · 364 词 · 3 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

官方样题 · British Council · Academic Practice Test 2 · Miles Davis · Q14–19 · PDF 第 1, 2 页

Choose the correct heading for each paragraph from the list of headings. Write the correct Roman numeral, i–ix. 本组保留原题号；同一标题不可重复使用。

DThough Davis’ trumpet playing may have sounded effortless and breezy, this ease rarely carried over into the rest of his life. The early 1950s, in particular, were a time of great personal turmoil. After returning from a stint in Paris, Davis suffered from prolonged depression, which he attributed to the unravelling of a number of relationships, including his romance with a French actress and some musical partnerships that ruptured as a result of creative disputes. Davis was also frustrated by his perception that he had been overlooked by the music critics, who were hailing the success of his collaborators and descendants in the ‘cool’ tradition, such as Gerry Mulligan and Dave Brubeck, but who afforded him little credit for introducing the cool sound in the first place.

EIn the latter decades of his career, Davis broke out of exclusive jazz settings and began to diversify his output across a range of musical styles. In the 1960s, he was influenced by early funk performers such as Sly and the Family Stone, which then expanded into the jazz-rock fusion genre – of which he was a frontrunner – in the 1970s. Electronic recording effects and electric instruments were incorporated into his sound. By the 1980s, Davis was pushing the boundaries further, covering pop anthems such as Cyndi Lauper’s Time After Time and Michael Jackson’s Human Nature, dabbling in hip hop, and even appearing in some movies.

FNot everyone was supportive of Davis’ change of tune. Compared to the recordings of his early career, universally applauded as linchpins of the jazz oeuvre, trumpeter Wynston Marsalis derided his fusion work as being ‘not true jazz’, and pianist Bill Evans denounced the ‘corrupting influence’ of record companies, noting that rock and pop ‘draw wider audiences’. In the face of this criticism Davis remained defiant, commenting that his earlier recordings were part of a moment in time that he had no ‘feel’ for any more. He firmly believed that remaining stylistically inert would have hampered his ability to develop new ways of producing music. From this perspective, Davis’ continual revamping of genre was not merely a rebellion, but an evolution, a necessary path that allowed him to release his full musical potential.

  • vii. Conflicted opinions over Davis’ earlier work

17. Paragraph D

18. Paragraph E

19. Paragraph F

对照答案，回到证据

第 17 题 · ix

关系破裂属个人困境，音乐合作冲突和被评论家忽视属职业困境，两半共同满足ix。

his romance with a French actress and some musical partnerships that ruptured as a result of creative disputes.

第 18 题 · iv

funk→fusion→pop→hip hop是扩展音乐方向，年份本身不是主旨。

began to diversify his output across a range of musical styles.

第 19 题 · vi

批评是引入，末句说明变化释放音乐潜能；重点是为何必须变化而非只列别人不赞成。

remaining stylistically inert would have hampered his ability to develop new ways of producing music.

核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

这三段把听起来轻松的音乐与并不轻松的人生并置，继而写风格跨界引起的争论。结尾从戴维斯自己的创作观解释变化：继续发展对他比维持旧风格更重要。

D

Though Davis’ trumpet playing may have sounded effortless and breezy, this ease rarely carried over into the rest of his life. The early 1950s, in particular, were a time of great personal turmoil. After returning from a stint in Paris, Davis suffered from prolonged depression, which he attributed to the unravelling of a number of relationships, including his romance with a French actress and some musical partnerships that ruptured as a result of creative disputes. Davis was also frustrated by his perception that he had been overlooked by the music critics, who were hailing the success of his collaborators and descendants in the ‘cool’ tradition, such as Gerry Mulligan and Dave Brubeck, but who afforded him little credit for introducing the cool sound in the first place.

D段先区分演奏给人的轻松感与个人生活。文中把五十年代初的抑郁与人际、合作关系破裂联系起来，同时交代他认为评论界忽视了自己的贡献。which he attributed to与his perception都保留了当事人的解释和感受，不能改写成已经独立证实的全部成因。

E

In the latter decades of his career, Davis broke out of exclusive jazz settings and began to diversify his output across a range of musical styles. In the 1960s, he was influenced by early funk performers such as Sly and the Family Stone, which then expanded into the jazz-rock fusion genre – of which he was a frontrunner – in the 1970s. Electronic recording effects and electric instruments were incorporated into his sound. By the 1980s, Davis was pushing the boundaries further, covering pop anthems such as Cyndi Lauper’s Time After Time and Michael Jackson’s Human Nature, dabbling in hip hop, and even appearing in some movies.

E段按年代呈现创作范围的扩展：放克影响、爵士与摇滚融合、电子效果和电声乐器，随后涉及流行歌曲、嘻哈和电影。diversify不是放弃音乐，而是让创作跨越更多风格。段落为下一段的批评提供具体背景。

F

Not everyone was supportive of Davis’ change of tune. Compared to the recordings of his early career, universally applauded as linchpins of the jazz oeuvre, trumpeter Wynston Marsalis derided his fusion work as being ‘not true jazz’, and pianist Bill Evans denounced the ‘corrupting influence’ of record companies, noting that rock and pop ‘draw wider audiences’. In the face of this criticism Davis remained defiant, commenting that his earlier recordings were part of a moment in time that he had no ‘feel’ for any more. He firmly believed that remaining stylistically inert would have hampered his ability to develop new ways of producing music. From this perspective, Davis’ continual revamping of genre was not merely a rebellion, but an evolution, a necessary path that allowed him to release his full musical potential.

F段呈现对跨界的不同判断：有人认为融合不是真正的爵士，也有人把变化归因于唱片公司的商业影响。戴维斯则说，早期作品属于自己已没有同样感受的过去；原地不动会限制创作。结尾的From this perspective限定了“演进而非仅仅叛逆”这一评价的观察角度。

词语与搭配

carried over into

延续到；影响到另一领域

carry over强调一种状态从原来的范围延伸出去；此处否定音乐的轻松感同样存在于他的生活中。

diversify his output

使自己的作品类型多样化

output在此指创作产出；diversify强调种类和方向增加，不等于每种尝试都得到肯定。

draw wider audiences

吸引范围更广的观众

draw在此是吸引；wider侧重覆盖面更广，不能据此推断作品艺术价值高低。

In the face of this criticism

面对这些批评

in the face of可接困难、反对等；this criticism回指对跨界作品及商业影响的批评。

句子精读

Though Davis’ trumpet playing may have sounded effortless and breezy, this ease rarely carried over into the rest of his life.

虽然戴维斯的小号演奏可能听起来轻松自在，但这种轻松感很少延续到他生活的其他方面。

Though引出让步；may have sounded描述听众可能获得的听觉印象，而非断言演奏过程毫不费力。this ease承接effortless and breezy的感受，rarely限制延续发生的频率。

He firmly believed that remaining stylistically inert would have hampered his ability to develop new ways of producing music.

他坚信，如果风格一直停滞不变，就会妨碍他发展新的音乐创作方式。

He指戴维斯。remaining stylistically inert是动名词结构，充当宾语从句的主语；would have hampered表达他对未选择的停滞状态的判断。句子陈述他的信念，不是关于所有艺术家的普遍定律。

这篇材料里可用于写作的表达

draw wider audiences

吸引范围更广的观众

可具体说明线上娱乐的可达性；观众范围扩大不等于线下场所失去全部文化价值。

用于写作：自编例句，直接回应线上娱乐的覆盖范围优势；can和especially保留条件，也为讨论剧院独有的现场体验留下空间。

读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。

官方样题 · Cambridge Academic Reading official sample · Dung beetles · PDF 第 1, 2 页

Label the tunnels on the diagram below using words from the box. Write your answers in boxes 6–8. 按原图位置作答，词框完整保留。

原官方样题完整保留连续三段，图示与下一组表格为同篇材料的不同正式题组，不计作两篇独立原文。

1Introducing dung beetles into a pasture is a simple process: approximately 1,500 beetles are released, a handful at a time, into fresh cow pats in the cow pasture. The beetles immediately disappear beneath the pats digging and tunnelling and, if they successfully adapt to their new environment, soon become a permanent, self-sustaining part of the local ecology. In time they multiply and within three or four years the benefits to the pasture are obvious.

2Dung beetles work from the inside of the pat so they are sheltered from predators such as birds and foxes. Most species burrow into the soil and bury dung in tunnels directly underneath the pats, which are hollowed out from within. Some large species originating from France excavate tunnels to a depth of approximately 30 cm below the dung pat. These beetles make sausage-shaped brood chambers along the tunnels. The shallowest tunnels belong to a much smaller Spanish species that buries dung in chambers that hang like fruit from the branches of a pear tree. South African beetles dig narrow tunnels of approximately 20 cm below the surface of the pat. Some surface-dwelling beetles, including a South African species, cut perfectly-shaped balls from the pat, which are rolled away and attached to the bases of plants.

3For maximum dung burial in spring, summer and autumn, farmers require a variety of species with overlapping periods of activity. In the cooler environments of the state of Victoria, the large French species (2.5 cms long), is matched with smaller (half this size), temperate-climate Spanish species. The former are slow to recover from the winter cold and produce only one or two generations of offspring from late spring until autumn. The latter, which multiply rapidly in early spring, produce two to five generations annually. The South African ball-rolling species, being a sub-tropical beetle, prefers the climate of northern and coastal New South Wales where it commonly works with the South African tunneling species. In warmer climates, many species are active for longer periods of the year.

核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

这段材料先写蜣螂如何被引入牧场，再从地下隧道、育幼室和滚粪球的位置解释不同工作方式，最后把物种差异联系到季节配合。理解重点是条件、空间关系和形态之间的联系。

1

Introducing dung beetles into a pasture is a simple process: approximately 1,500 beetles are released, a handful at a time, into fresh cow pats in the cow pasture. The beetles immediately disappear beneath the pats digging and tunnelling and, if they successfully adapt to their new environment, soon become a permanent, self-sustaining part of the local ecology. In time they multiply and within three or four years the benefits to the pasture are obvious.

第1段说明引入过程及建立种群的条件：把甲虫少量分批放入新鲜牛粪后，它们会向下挖掘；只有成功适应新环境，才会形成能自行维持的本地生态组成。三四年后收益明显是文中描述的时间尺度，不能略去适应条件。

2

Dung beetles work from the inside of the pat so they are sheltered from predators such as birds and foxes. Most species burrow into the soil and bury dung in tunnels directly underneath the pats, which are hollowed out from within. Some large species originating from France excavate tunnels to a depth of approximately 30 cm below the dung pat. These beetles make sausage-shaped brood chambers along the tunnels. The shallowest tunnels belong to a much smaller Spanish species that buries dung in chambers that hang like fruit from the branches of a pear tree. South African beetles dig narrow tunnels of approximately 20 cm below the surface of the pat. Some surface-dwelling beetles, including a South African species, cut perfectly-shaped balls from the pat, which are rolled away and attached to the bases of plants.

第2段从共同的遮蔽位置写到不同物种的挖掘形态：法国种向下挖约30厘米并形成香肠状育幼室；西班牙种较浅，育幼室如树枝上悬挂的果实；南非种既有挖窄隧道的，也有把粪球滚离粪堆并固定在植物基部的。文中的形状比喻帮助理解位置，不表示真的长成果实。

3

原文片段 · 1It is by now a truism that the story of human evolution is being rethought. Discoveries have come thick and fast over the last decade or so, and these have forced us to rethink many crucial points, such as how old our species is - about 300,000 years old as opposed to 200,000 - and what extinct hominins, such as our cousins the Neanderthals, were really like. But because there are so many species and eras involved, it's hard to discern the common threads linking them.

原文片段 · 2However, I do think it's possible to draw out some overall messages from the blizzard of archaeological finds in recent years. Two things stand out to me. One is the growing evidence that many supposedly 'advanced' behaviours, such as architecture and art, can be traced much further back in time than we thought, often to hominin species that existed before modern humans. And the other is that we have badly misunderstood gender roles in prehistoric societies, imposing patriarchal values onto cultures that had very different ideas about how women should behave.

原文片段 · 3Let's start with architecture. At Kalambo Falls in Zambia, researchers found buried logs that had been shaped with stone tools so that they interlocked. They seem to have once been part of a larger structure, perhaps a building. This would be unsurprising if they weren't 476,000 years old. That's almost 200,000 years before our species, Homo sapiens, evolved. Extinct hominins also managed to settle in extreme places. For instance, we now know that extinct hominins such as the Denisovans lived on the frozen heights of high-altitude regions 200,000 years ago - upending the old notion that such environments were only settled by modern humans around 3,600 years ago.

材料精读 · 内容与词句

作者把大量考古发现归纳成两条需要重看的认识：某些被视为先进的行为比过去想象的更早出现，对史前性别分工的看法也可能受当代预设影响。这里主要展开建筑和极端环境定居的例子，注意区分发现本身与研究者对用途的推测。

原文片段 · 1

It is by now a truism that the story of human evolution is being rethought. Discoveries have come thick and fast over the last decade or so, and these have forced us to rethink many crucial points, such as how old our species is - about 300,000 years old as opposed to 200,000 - and what extinct hominins, such as our cousins the Neanderthals, were really like. But because there are so many species and eras involved, it's hard to discern the common threads linking them.

接连出现的发现改变了对人类起源年代及已灭绝人族成员的理解，但物种和年代众多，整体联系并不容易辨认。truism 表示已经被反复承认的说法；common threads 是贯穿材料的共同线索，作者接下来要从碎片发现中提炼这些联系。

原文片段 · 2

However, I do think it's possible to draw out some overall messages from the blizzard of archaeological finds in recent years. Two things stand out to me. One is the growing evidence that many supposedly 'advanced' behaviours, such as architecture and art, can be traced much further back in time than we thought, often to hominin species that existed before modern humans. And the other is that we have badly misunderstood gender roles in prehistoric societies, imposing patriarchal values onto cultures that had very different ideas about how women should behave.

作者明确以 I do think 和 to me 提出自己的归纳：建筑、艺术等行为的历史可能追溯到现代人之前；史前女性角色则被后来的父权观念误读。supposedly 给 advanced 加上距离感，提醒读者所谓先进本身也带有分类与评价。

原文片段 · 3

Let's start with architecture. At Kalambo Falls in Zambia, researchers found buried logs that had been shaped with stone tools so that they interlocked. They seem to have once been part of a larger structure, perhaps a building. This would be unsurprising if they weren't 476,000 years old. That's almost 200,000 years before our species, Homo sapiens, evolved. Extinct hominins also managed to settle in extreme places. For instance, we now know that extinct hominins such as the Denisovans lived on the frozen heights of high-altitude regions 200,000 years ago - upending the old notion that such environments were only settled by modern humans around 3,600 years ago.

赞比亚木构件的加工与咬合显示它们可能属于更大的结构，但 perhaps a building 仍是对用途的推测。476,000年前的年代使发现尤其突出，因为比现代人出现还早。高海拔地区的古人族居住证据则挑战了这类环境很晚才被占据的旧想法。

词语与搭配

come thick and fast

大量而接连不断地出现

形容发现出现得多且频繁；是较生动的固定表达，不是说发现物本身很厚。

the common threads

共同线索

threads 比喻连接不同发现的主题；作者想理解它们共同改变了什么认识。

can be traced much further back in time

可以追溯到久远得多的过去

be traced back 表示追溯起源；much 修饰比较级 further，强调与旧估计的差距。

imposing patriarchal values onto cultures

把父权价值观强加到其他文化的解释上

这里指用后来研究者的观念解读古代文化，并非说这些研究者真的改变了史前社会。

句子精读

One is the growing evidence that many supposedly 'advanced' behaviours, such as architecture and art, can be traced much further back in time than we thought, often to hominin species that existed before modern humans.

其中一点是，越来越多证据显示，建筑和艺术等许多所谓先进的行为，可以追溯到比我们原先想象久远得多的年代，往往追溯到现代人出现之前就已存在的人族物种。

One 指作者归纳出的两条认识之一。第一个 that 引出 evidence 的具体内容，such as 插入例子；than we thought 给出比较基准。最后的 that existed 修饰 hominin species，限定这些物种所处的时代。

At Kalambo Falls in Zambia, researchers found buried logs that had been shaped with stone tools so that they interlocked.

在赞比亚的卡兰博瀑布，研究人员发现了埋藏的木料，这些木料曾用石器加工，从而能够相互咬合。

that had been shaped 修饰 logs，过去完成时表示加工早于研究人员发现。so that 引出加工所达到的目的或效果，they 回指木料。句子先报告材料及加工特征，后文才推测它们可能的用途。
